buyer: LPs - family offices, HNW individuals, seed-capital allocators
pain: SMID as an asset class is under-covered and arguably under-valued
v1: A fund. There is no crude v1 - this is the point.
channel: Her network plus her father's and husband's contacts, none of whom allocate to first-time managers as a matter of course
verdict: Weak as a thing to start now - year-one revenue is structurally zero. As a year-four destination the economics are the best of the three.

why.distribution: Her network and her father's China energy contacts could produce an anchor LP conversation, but LPs for a first-time manager are a different game from research buyers, and family introductions are a handful of conversations rather than a channel.
why.demand: No evidence anyone will allocate to a first-time manager with no audited track record. The pain is inferred.
why.fmf: She is an analyst, not a portfolio manager with a track record. Fund management, fundraising and compliance are three new jobs learned simultaneously.
why.revenue_structure: A management fee is the best recurring revenue there is - contracted, annual, and it renews by default.
why.defensibility: Track record compounds and AUM is sticky, but only once both exist.
why.leverage: Capital scales without labour - genuinely the highest-leverage structure available to her.
why.capital: FCA authorisation or an appointed-representative arrangement under a regulatory host: ~£25-60k/yr plus setup, or £100k+ all-in for full authorisation.
why.time_to_revenue: Regulatory gate plus a fundraise. Well over twelve months before a fee is collected.
why.tailwind: SMID is out of favour and active management fees are compressing, against a genuine value-opportunity narrative.
why.ceiling: Year-one revenue is zero by construction. The criterion asks about year one, and the answer is nothing.

ceiling_arithmetic: 2% on £25m AUM = £500k/yr - the best economics of the three ideas, and unreachable in year one. Authorisation takes 6-12 months and a first-time-manager fundraise takes years. Year-one revenue: £0. The score reflects 'as a thing to start now', not the destination.
carries: The only one of the three where the ceiling is genuinely large, and the revenue structure and leverage are the best available.
kills: Time-to-revenue at 0 and ceiling at 0. It is gated on a licence and a track record, neither of which she has, and both of which take years.
test: Not a two-week test. The right first step is to build the auditable thing the fund is gated on: a public, timestamped research record with tracked calls.
test_pass: A verifiable performance log that a seed allocator would take seriously after 24-36 months.
test_fail: n/a - this is a multi-year precondition, not an experiment.
reshape: Invert the order: publish free and build a timestamped, auditable track record while the institutional research subscription pays the bills. The research business funds year one; the public record makes the fund fundable in year four.
flags: Managing investments in the UK is FCA-regulated - appointed representative under a regulatory host (~£25-60k/yr plus setup) or full authorisation (6-12 months, £100k+). Publishing research on names later held and traded creates a conflict and market-abuse surface needing a personal-account-dealing and disclosure policy from day one.
